articles.body:
Welcome to IGN's guide to Wave Race: Blue Storm, the GameCube sequel to the Nintendo 64 classic Wave Race 64. Though Blue Storm was not coded by Nintendo's internal EAD development team, the game's US developer NST has done a great job bringing the wet racing fun to the GameCube.

But don't mistake Blue Storm for a carbon copy of its predecessor. The controls are much deeper (and much more complex), and a new trick/boost system opens the door for all new strategies and shortcuts.

This guide contains detailed strategies on each track in the game. Since the track layouts differ from difficulty to difficulty, you will find a dedicated page for each course variation in the Track Strategies section.

IGN's Wave Race: Blue Storm Guide was originally written by Peer Schneider as a mini-guide in 2001. The pages were published manually as flat html on IGN Guides. The text images were much later imported into a wiki cms and opened up to user edits. In 2026, with the release of the game as part of GameCube Classics on Nintendo Switch 2, the original author went back and fixed broken pages and guide issues to bring the guide up to modern IGN guide standards.

articles.title: Aspen Lake - Normal - Wave Race: Blue Storm Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Wave Race: Blue Storm at IGN: walkthroughs, items, maps, video tips, and strategies
articles.body:
Though its name has changed, Aspen Lake is another returning favorite from the original Wave Race console game. Like in the predecessor, the tranquil lake never kicks up nasty waves, but the buoy locations as well as some strategically placed rocks make for a challenging race. Like Southern Island, Aspen Lake features changing water levels -- but in this case they're entirely dependent on the weather conditions. The differences between the weather conditions are more pronounced on the higher difficulty levels, but there are some subtle changes on Normal, too. So pay attention to the weather when you choose Aspen as your next track.

Don't worry about waves on this stage. It's all about the buoys this time around. Start off with a boost and head towards the first red marker. Pass it and head straight toward the right side of the rock ahead of you. Pass it on the right, then turn left and go around the red buoy. The next series of buoys is as straightforward as they come. You can pass them with very little turning. As you enter the northernmost section of the track, turn slightly left and head right for the flat rock in between the yellow and red buoys. This rock won't knock you off your racer, so simply skip over it.

You are now in the perfect position to take a fancy shortcut. A green-brown natural ramp is straight ahead of you. If you take it correctly, you can bypass the small wooden bridge that would otherwise be too close to the water level to let you get through. It's a little tricky if you don't go up the ramp just right. Aim just to the right of the two trees on the left of the bridge. When you're in the air, either push the nose of your racer down, or hold L and R at the same time. This will let you dive underneath the bridge and emerge on the other side. If you're having trouble lining up for the jump, just go around the bridge on the right. There is no shame in playing it safe and winning a race.

Either way, you will now have to navigate a series of buoys next to a small waterfall that causes ripples in the water. Since they're so close together, save your turbo until you get to a yellow marker right in front of a bunch of lily pads towards the left (they're a camp ground on the right). Hit your turbo boost as you pass the lilies and head straight for the area just to the right of the left pole of the start gate. Yes, you will miss a red buoy over on the right, but it's faster this way. There is a small wooden pier with a boat right before the start gate. Jump the right side of the pier and you will hit a hidden turbo boost

You can use this same route for all three laps and finish the race this way. Expert players who are not at risk of missing buoys by accident can also try a different approach. When you start the race, head toward the left (there's another patch of lilies there) and instead of going around the red buoy on the right, hit turbo and miss it on purpose. Cut across the lake to the second yellow marker ahead (you will miss another red buoy) and pass the third red buoy correctly on the right. You can still take the shortcut right before the start gate (as detailed in the paragraph above) twice. But since you can't miss any more buoys in lap 3, you will have to remember not to miss the final red buoy on purpose.

There are of course other variations of purposely bypassing buoys to better your time that you can try out. Have fun finding them.

Now this is the lake level we learned to love in Wave Race 64. Cloudy really means foggy in this case. Your view is severely restricted by mist in the first lap of the race, but the morning fog burns off as you head into the second lap. By lap 3, the view is clear. The water level remains the same so follow the above strategies.

Although the rain obscures your vision it doesn't have any impact on the water level on this setting. The rain stops on lap 3. Follow the basic instructions above.

The strong rain increases the water level with every lap and creates a choppier water surface. The first lap is pretty much the same as the before, but after you finish the first lap, the water level rises. Some of the rocks that were visible on the better weather conditions are now submerged, so if anything, completion of this level is now easier. There is of course one catch. It will now be slightly tougher to dive under the bridge on lap 2, but it's still doable. You can alternatively jump over it as well, but you'll need a turbo boost for most riders. On lap 3, the water level is now high enough to cover most sticks and rocks. Forget about diving underneath the bridge, though. Simply jump over it with the help of the ramp. If you bypass the red buoy before the finish line, note that the boost ramp still works even when it's nearly submerged.

The water level is at its highest, but it doesn't change during the race. The same rules apply as on the other conditions, but remember that you should jump over the bridge at all times. As on "Rainy," the boost ramp still works, even when it's submerged.

Boost Points: You can safely boost anywhere you like, except for passages with many buoys and the bridge dive part (if the water level is low).

The hidden turbo ramp is right in front of the start/finish gate next to the bait shop. Simply aim for the area next to the boat and you'll catch an extra boost.

The wooden planks that stick vertically out of the water can be broken by smashing into them. Try to mow them all down.

Nothing screams Blue Storm pro more than breaking the start gate. You need a lot of speed to do this and it's easier to do with the faster riders, but the basic idea is to launch yourself off the boost ramp and hit the horizontal part of the gate with your head. It'll break and leave a gaping hole. Makes for nice replays, too.

...that the fish are jumping out of the water on good weather conditions?

...that a flock of Canada Geese flies around just like in Wave Race 64?

...that there are bears on the shore (and especially around the camp grounds)?

articles.summary: This Southeast-Asian course is a good first choice to pick when you enter any championship. The different weather conditions don't really affect the
articles.body:
This Southeast-Asian course is a good first choice to pick when you enter any championship. The different weather conditions don't really affect the course much, so it doesn't matter which one you choose. The water level remains the same and there are no notable shortcuts. It's a safe ride all around.

Time your start right so that you get a turbo boost right off the bat. Since you're on a long straight you should boost right away. If you didn't get a turbo, you should at the latest get one after passing the second yellow buoy. You can now safely engage the boost as you turn. Get ready for a long left - but don't oversteer. Until you're completely comfortable with the controls stay in the middle of the track. When you're confident enough, get as close as possible to the left rock wall to shave off a few nanoseconds of your lap time, but don't accidentally turn into the cove with the sign. As you approach the yellow buoy around the corner, make a wide left turn to set yourself up perfectly for the short slalom section that follows. Try to steer as little as possible to maneuver around the buoys. Make a sharp left turn after the last red buoy on this straight and get ready for the final stretch.

If you've got it, engage your boost as you turn onto the final straight. If you're confident enough, you can do this even before you pass the red buoy before the corner. This will ensure that your turbo is full again in no time. It takes some practice, but boosting while turning is a valuable technique for pro racers. The only danger is that you over steer while boosting and you will smash into the wall to the left. To prevent this, turn only lightly (don't pull back on the stick or lean).

Stick to the left side after you pass the buoys. There is a small boost ramp next to the houses right after the finish line. Take the ramp for a free boost. If you want, you can pull off a quick trick in the air to build up your turbo.

The track is virtually identical on partially cloudy weather conditions. The sky looks a little more drab and the water is just slightly less smooth, but not enough to negatively affect your racing technique.

The race starts out in the rain, but the weather calms down in time for the final lap. Visibility isn't as good as in clear conditions, but other than that it's the same deal as before. Watch out for some minor waves in the turns and on the final stretch. The latter may make it a bit harder to straighten yourself after using your turbo. Don't be afraid to use the shoulder buttons to avoid smashing into obstacles.

Visibility suffers notably under rainy and foggy conditions, but the course and water level remain unchanged. The waves and increased chop make it easier to screw up and make it slightly harder to set new lap records, but if you follow the basic strategies outlined for sunny weather you shouldn't have any problems.

You don't get to play Stormy on Normal mode very often, so consider yourself lucky if you encounter it in a championship race. The overall visibility is actually better here than under rainy or partially rainy conditions as the fog is notably absent, but the waves are more than twice the size. But since the higher waves are confined to the open areas they won't give you much trouble. Race Stormy as you would race Clear. Just don't get distracted by the rain drops hitting your TV.

Shortcuts: There are no special shortcuts that let you bypass sections of the track and the buoy placement doesn't allow for much cheating. However, if you boost late in the long wide left turn after the start line, you can effectively skip the first (yellow) buoy of the straight "slalom" section. As you come around the turn, stick closely to the second protruding rock formation, but instead of turning left to go around the yellow buoy, simply go straight and head for the right side of the following red buoy. You will of course incur a "miss"

articles.title: Nintendo Switch Online’s N64 and Sega Genesis ‘expansion pack’ launches October 25th for $49.99 per year
articles.summary: Nintendo has announced the pricing for its Switch Online + Expansion Pack subscription service: it’ll cost $49.99 per year for a single subscription, or $79.99 for a family membership. In addition to N64 and Genesis games, it’ll also include access to the new paid Animal Crossing DLC.
articles.body: Nintendo has announced the price and release for its upcoming Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack subscription tier, which adds Nintendo 64 games, Sega Genesis games, and bundled access to the new paid Animal Crossing: New Horizons — Happy Home Paradise DLC. It’ll cost $49.99 per year for an individual subscription or $79.99 for a shared family membership. The service will officially launch on October 25th. Those prices are a big jump from the regular Switch Online subscription, which costs $19.99 per year for a single membership or $34.99 per year for a family subscription. The Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack subscription tier offers the same benefits as the standard Switch Online service — including online multiplayer, classic NES and SNES games, cloud saves, and other perks. [Image: But the Expansion Pack subscription also adds access to other retro titles from the Nintendo 64 and Sega Genesis. Today’s pricing announcement included news that the premium subscription service would also bring bundled access to the new paid Animal Crossing: New Horizons DLC (which is set to cost $24.99 on its own). At launch, the Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack service will include several of the most popular N64 games, including Super Mario 64, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, and Mario Kart 64. Additional titles are also planned for the future, like Banjo-Kazooie, Pokémon Snap, The Legend of Zelda: Majora’s Mask, and Paper Mario. The higher $49.99 per year price point also puts Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack more in line with other major subscription costs from competitors like Sony and Microsoft (PlayStation Plus and Xbox Live Gold both cost $59.99 per year, albeit with fewer perks than Nintendo’s retro game offerings). In addition to the Switch Online + Expansion Pack details, Nintendo also opened preorders for the matching wireless Nintendo 64 and Sega Genesis controllers (each $49.99, with USB-C charging) that its selling to go with the new retro games. The new controllers are set to ship alongside the new service on October 25th. Update October 15th, 10:44AM ET: Added release date information. Update October 15th, 1:11PM ET: Added N64 and Genesis controller information.

articles.title: This keyboard and trackball combo is for the tinkerers
articles.summary: ZSA launched the Navigator trackball to accompany its Voyager mechanical keyboard, and they are great desk upgrades if you love to tinker and customize.
articles.body: Do you love to tinker with your keyboard layout? Do you love trackballs and think that one that attaches magnetically to your keyboard would be the coolest thing ever? Are you willing to completely blow up your setup in pursuit of possibly huge — or possibly marginal — gains in comfort or efficiency? Then I have a keyboard and trackball recommendation for you, with some caveats. In early September, I started dabbling with ZSA’s Voyager keyboard and new Navigator trackball attachment. The Voyager is a low-profile, wired, split mechanical keyboard with 52 hot-swappable keys in a columnar-staggered layout. When you buy it, you can pick from one of four types of Kailh Choc v1 switches. The one shipped to me has Pro Red linear switches, which feel a little mushy in comparison to the Cherry MX Brown switches I’m used to. The Voyager has RGB lights, too, if you want to add a little color to your days. [Product: ZSA Voyager and Navigator | The Voyager came out in 2023, but the interesting new thing is the Navigator trackball, which was announced in August. The trackball module snaps magnetically onto either the right or left half of your Voyager, just above the thumb cluster. (You pick which side at checkout.) The ball, which comes in a color that I might best describe as “trackball red,” feels really smooth to roll around. It’s nice having it right next to your typing fingers, because it means you barely have to move them from your keyboard. ZSA says the Voyager is “designed with a laptop in mind,” and I can see why: the keyboard is small enough to toss in a bag if you want to bring your laptop somewhere but would prefer to type on a more custom setup. (It even comes with a carrying case.) If you want to ever-so-slightly tent the two sides, the keyboard comes with four little nubs that attach magnetically to the bottom. I mostly used the Voyager flat and was fine with it, though I would have preferred if the included nubs were able to tent the keyboard at a steeper angle like other ergonomic keyboards that I’ve used. You can buy a tripod mount that lets you totally customize the tilt and pitch angle, or even mount the Voyager halves to your desk or the arms of your chair. But you can also make or buy other magnetic tenting accessories and attach them to the bottom of the keyboard yourself — you can even remove the magnets from the included nubs to use them in your own solution. [Image: The tenting nub. The real magic of the Voyager and Navigator, as with ZSA’s Moonlander keyboard that I reviewed in 2021, is how much you can customize them using ZSA’s Oryx configurator software. The software lets you program any key to be any other key, or a macro, or a media playback button, or even a mouse click. Keys can have different functions when tapped, held, double-tapped, or tapped and held. You can even set different layers of keys that are activated by pressing another key. This type of customization is pretty standard for enthusiast keyboards, but I’ve found Oryx’s software to be particularly easy to use. Once you’ve decided on a layout, you can flash it to the keyboard using ZSA’s Keymapp app. I should say here that the Voyager and Navigator are not cheap. The Voyager is $365, while the Navigator is $169, so the total cost is $534. If you want the tripod mount, that costs an additional $89 — and the tripod itself isn’t included. These are accessories for people who have very specific typing needs or who really want to go deep on customizing their tools. [Image: ZSA’s Voyager keyboard without the wires. This is a wired keyboard; it has one cable to go to your computer and another connecting the two halves. Usually, I fit both of those criteria. My typical current setup is a split ergonomic keyboard, the 95-key Kinesis Freestyle Pro, and a vertical ergonomic mouse, the Contour Unimouse. I taught myself Colemak after spending my entire life on QWERTY. At one point I alternated between a regular mouse and a full-sized trackball. For a while I used a rollermouse as my daily driver. And I went really deep with the Moonlander, even making a layer dedicated to shortcuts for watching YouTube videos. I’m no stranger to the fun and suffering of switching up my computing input devices, or to going to great lengths for a more ergonomic setup. But with the 52-key Voyager, I just keep finding myself a few keys short of a layout that feels right to me. The thing I missed the most was a reliable set of arrow keys. I could use a layer or a fancy shortcut of some kind, but they’re so critical to my day-to-day work of futzing with text and cursors that I don’t want to trip over myself to get to them. And the trackball module doesn’t come with mouse keys. I put the left and right mouse click buttons under my thumb on the left side of the keyboard. But that took away two keys on the default layer I could use for something else. [Image: Look at that red! Unlike my Kinesis, which is essentially a standard staggered keyboard that’s chopped in half, the Voyager is a columnar keyboard, meaning the keys for each finger are in a straight line above and below each other, and my fingers sometimes got tangled up when I used it. The Moonlander is also a columnar keyboard, and that took a couple weeks to get comfortable with, too. I’m going to be honest: I got frustrated with the Voyager after a week and didn’t use it at all over a busy stretch of events like the iPhone 17 launch or my trip to Meta Connect. In my work, I have to be a very fast writer and communicator, and as fun as the Voyager and Navigator are to use, I was much slower with them than my usual setup. While I would love to spend hours after work or on a weekend perfecting my setup, as a father to a very busy toddler, I just don’t have the time or energy to make that happen. This might just be a me thing. I think before my kid was born, I could have gone all-in on making the Voyager and the Navigator work. I did it with the Moonlander, after all, which has a similar columnar layout, and I only switched away from that because I realized that the Kinesis fit my hands better long-term. And to my great surprise while writing this draft, I settled back into the Voyager and Navigator really easily. I still have issues with my layout, but I thought coming back cold from a long break was going to be a lot more difficult. For the right person, I think the Voyager and Navigator could be an awesome desk upgrade to tinker with and customize. I’m not that person right now. But I want to be again — having a trackball attached directly to my keyboard is a whole lot of fun.

articles.title: The Best LEGO Gifts to Buy For Adults in 2026
articles.summary: Looking for a gift for the adult LEGO builder in your life? Look no further – we've gathered all the best sets this year.
articles.body:
There has never been a better time to be a LEGO Adult, which means there has never been a better time to be someone looking for a gift for a LEGO Adult—even if that adult LEGO fan is you.

In 2026, LEGO has released hundreds of new sets globally, across dozens of different themes. Some of the most popular adult collector lines include Icons, Botanical, Art, and Architecture, but it’s the licensed entertainment lines that tend to get us the most excited at IGN. LEGO has teamed up with some of pop culture’s biggest brands to bring nerds story-driven builds in the worlds of Lord of the Rings, Harry Potter, Pokémon, and more.

As we head into the holiday season, we’ve compiled a list of must-have sets for LEGO Adults. Most of these sets were released in 2026, and have been amongst the best-reviewed builds of the year. We’ve prioritized recommending LEGO Adult sets at different price points, so if the recommended set is above (or below) your budget, be sure to read the description for another suggestion within that franchise.

Here’s a look at every set in the article. Click on any that look good to you, or keep on reading to find out more info about each set.

LEGO Hogsmeade™ Village – Collectors' Edition

LEGO Zelda: Ocarina of Time - The Final Battle

LEGO Iron Man Mark 3 Collectors’ Edition

The Lord of the Rings Minas Tirith LEGO Set

At 8,278 pieces, Minas Tirith is the largest Lord of the Rings build released yet. LEGO Model Designers employed a hybrid-scale model to recreate the grandeur of the Gondor capital. The exterior of the city uses minifig-scale, microscale, and nanoscale to create a forced perspective effect—similar to the strategy Peter Jackson employed to represent different sized Lord of the Rings characters from mostly similarly sized human actors on the big screen. The detailed build comes with 10 minifigs, in case you need to stage The Battle of Pelennor Fields.

If this massive Lord of the Rings set is too expensive or just plain too big for your giftee, consider the Sauron Helmet set , a 538-piece build that makes for an intimidating office display.

Following the success of brick-build recreations of class game consoles like NES (retired), Atari 2600 (retired), and SEGA Genesis , LEGO has released a near 1:1 scale LEGO model of PlayStation . At 1,911 pieces, the retro build includes two interior dioramas inspired by classic games, making it a fun display piece.

If the PlayStation set is a little out of your price range, the 421-piece Game Boy build offers a smaller set that taps into the same sense of gaming nostalgia. Check out our thoughts on the build and our interview with the LEGO designer .

Ever since LEGO’s Pokémon licensing deal was announced in 2025, fans have been gearing up to catch them all. This past year was the big LEGO Pokémon launch, and the star of the show was arguably Eevee . The small, 587-piece build punches above its weight. LEGO Model Designers really nailed the cuteness of Eevee’s design, from the big eyes to the posable ears to the bushy tail, making it a good display piece once finished.

For gift-givers looking to spend a bit more on the Pokémon fan in their life, the 6,838-piece Venusaur, Charizard, and Blastoise set gives you three Kanto Region Evolutions for one display.

For all the readers (and the film adaptation watchers) out there, LEGO released a microscale replica of the interstellar spacecraft from Project Hail Mary . What makes this 830-piece build so rewarding is the functionality of the finished product; by rotating the crank, the spaceship shifts from flight mode to centrifuge mode. It looks super cool, and elevates a cool LEGO display for an office or den into an interactive adventure. If the LEGO readers in your life aren’t sci-fi fans, try gifting them one of the toy company’s book nooks . These builds are designed to nestle cozily between volumes on a bookshelf. While most are based on specific books, such as the Harry Potter-themed Dumbledore’s Office , the latest release is a Bookstore: Book Nook . The two-story (no pun intended) bookstore setting, complete with spiral staircase and plenty of tomes, works for readers of any genre.

Zelda: Ocarina of Time - The Final Battle LEGO Set

Nintendo’s 2026 remake of the legendary Nintendo 64 game Zelda: Ocarina of Time launched in November, and quickly became one of the best-selling games of the year. LEGO’s Ocarina of Time - The Final Battle set commemorates this important game milestone by depicting the climactic showdown between Link, Zelda, and Navi and final boss beast Ganon. Our reviewer Seth G. Macy particularly loved minifig Ganondorf’s cape, the build’s lever mechanism, and the designers’ choice to go print over decal. There are plenty of Nintendo LEGO sets for fans to enjoy; we also recommend the Mario Kart - Luigi & Mach 8 set , a sibling follow-up to Mario & Standard Kart .

LEGO Iron Man Mark 3 Collectors’ Edition LEGO Set

If you have any friends who still haven’t recovered from the “I love you 3000” days of the MCU, get them the Iron Man Mark 3 Collectors’ Edition set . With 1,297 total pieces, builders can lovingly recreate the iconic suit from the Infinity Saga, and then display the figure for eternity. If the Marvel fans in your life skew more sinister and have less time on their hands, we recommend the 413-piece Venom Bust set , complete with searching (and removable) tongue.

LEGO and Star Wars go together like blue milk and ronto wraps, which makes the Star Wars LEGO line particularly robust. One of the latest, greatest builds include a 1,544-piece Boba Fett set (the Fett set, for short) that would look good on any bookshelf. If you’ve got the budget to burn, we also recommend the 1,809-piece Mandalorian N-1 Starfighter set or the Executor Super Star Destroyer —a massive, 6,130-piece set that is 4.5 feet long once assembled.

LEGO Stranger Things Creel House LEGO Set

We said goodbye to Stranger Things (at least the original series) at the end of 2025, but for those who want to revisit the world again and again, give the gift of the LEGO Stranger Things Creel House . The 2,593-piece comes with 13 minifigs that can be moved around the Gothic structure. While it looks boarded up from the outside, the building has removable boards and movable corners that reveal the supernatural secrets within. In addition to the minifigs, the set comes with Steve’s car, the WSQK radio van, and Will’s bicycle, expanding the world of this set beyond its build.

LEGO Captain Jack Sparrow’s Pirate Ship LEGO Set

The best LEGO sets include the most detail, and LEGO Captain Jack Sparrow’s Pirate Ship set is teeming with treasure in that way (and sometimes also literally). The 2,862-piece build comes with eight minifig characters from the popular Disney franchise, and incorporates cannons, swordplay, and a crow’s nest; the result is an adult LEGO set meant for both display and play. If your Disney friends skew more princess than pirate, try the 2,916-piece Beauty & the Beast Castle .

Sir Patrick Stewart was one of the great losses of 2026 . For Star Trek fans still working through their parasocial grief, consider gifting the Star Trek U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701-D set . The 3,600-piece build gives a home-office to Captain Jean-Luc Picard and his crew as they travel on the final frontier. This detailed replica of the legendary starship was the first ever LEGO Star Trek set, and includes a detachable saucer section in case of emergency. A newer Star Trek LEGO set option comes in the form of the Original Series Bridge set . With 1,701 pieces and eight minifigs, this is a good option for Star Trek LEGO fans who already have the TNG ship.

Hogsmeade™ Village – Collectors' Edition LEGO Set

Originally released in September 2025, the Hogsmeade Village - Collectors’ Edition is the ultimate winter-time Harry Potter build. A cozy re-creation of the village near Hogwarts where magical students can spend their weekends, the set includes 3,228 pieces and 12 minifigs (including a shocked Katie Bell, in case you want to act out the Half Blood Prince’s near-fatal cursing). It’s a big and pricey set; if you want something (a little) less expensive, you can pick up this micro-scale version of Diagon Alley . For more, check out our favorite LEGO Harry Potter sets , as well as the massive in-progress Hogwarts Castle , which comprises a whole bunch of sets released over the years.

What Makes a LEGO Set an Adult LEGO Set?

What do we mean by LEGO sets for adults , exactly? For starters, every LEGO set has a suggested age listed on the box, so we’re looking at the 18+ category here. But three things really separate LEGO sets for kids and sets for adults.

One is the complexity of the build itself. The more difficult it is to piece the set together, the higher the suggested age will be. Some sets have lots of fiddly little parts, or complicated mechanisms to facilitate movement, complete with rubber bands and cranks. How these things fit together can be hard to decipher from the printed instructions, making them better suited to adult builders.

Another reason a set is aimed at adults is that it’s intended for display rather than play. Sets for kids are generally meant to be picked up and played with. They’re sturdy enough to withstand lots of flopping around and bashing against other toys. Sets for adults are usually nicer to look at, and often come with an informational placard you can place next to them.

Finally, there’s the subject itself. Sets for adults can simply be boring for kids. Maybe it’s a botanical LEGO set meant to decorate your house. Maybe it’s a LEGO art set that re-creates a masterpiece, and when it’s built you can actually hang it on your wall. Or maybe it’s a retro-themed set that’s meant to spark nostalgia in builders of a certain age. These are all factors that play into a LEGO set’s age rating.

articles.title: 'Maybe It's Time': Sebastian Stan Fuels Fears Over Bucky's Fate in Avengers: Doomsday
articles.summary: Sebastian Stan has fueled MCU fan fears that Bucky Barnes could meet his end in Avengers: Doomsday after dropping a cryptic comment that "maybe it's time."
articles.body:
Sebastian Stan has fueled MCU fan fears that Bucky Barnes could meet his end in Avengers: Doomsday after dropping a cryptic comment that "maybe it's time."

With the massive crossover movie set to hit theaters next month, Stan was recently asked about Bucky's long-term future in the Marvel Cinematic Universe — and his response did little to calm nervous fans.

Having debuted all the way back in 2011's Captain America: The First Avenger, Bucky is one of the last remaining Phase One veterans still standing on the front lines. Now, with his old pal Steve Rogers back front and center for this next installment , many fans have long suspected Bucky's 15-year arc could be about to culminate with a long-awaited reunion followed by a tragic end.

Avengers: Doomsday Poster Montage Gallery

"I'm always happy to keep playing him," Stan said, while appearing recently on the Next Best Picture podcast. "I don't know if the decision's up to me, ultimately.

"I'm ready to take the character in all kinds of different ways," he continued, "but I can't make that decision, it's the powers that be. And I think they have a lot going on, they have a lot on their plate. Do I feel we've explored that character, there's nowhere else to go, I think we did our best? I do think we've done our best so far."

To be fair to Stan, after appearances in nine films and his own Disney+ spinoff, it's hard to know exactly where the character can continue to evolve. He is arguably the most experienced member of the New Avengers team, but this is a role that could also be provided by Yelena Belova. He has long since redeemed himself for his days as the Winter Soldier. And with Steve's story (presumably) wrapped up again with these latest Avengers movies, it's unclear what else there is for Bucky to do.

Stan has attempted to pitch a Bucky solo project to Marvel in the past — a thriller movie in the same vein as Denis Villeneuve-directed thriller Sicario — but noted again here that he had only received a non-commital response from MCU boss Kevin Feige.

"I don't think that that character totally got to fully live out his arc in the way that he has in the comics for instance, or that I've wanted," Stan concluded. "I'm always ready, but we're at that point now where I can feel it, he needs to either evolve somewhere, or maybe it's time. It's one of those."

While Bucky is beloved by MCU fans, Doomsday's apparent focus on the returning Steve Rogers provides a potentially unique narrative oppurtunity for the two characters' time-travelling bromance to reach an emotional conclusion. Will Bucky repay Steve for saving him by sacrificing his own life? Or will Doom simply kill him to upset Steve? Regardless of what happens, it's worth recalling something Chris Evans said recently of his character's own "brutal" arc in Doomsday :

"The Russos love beating up Steve Rogers," Evans remarked. "Their favourite thing to do is to just beat the crap out of him. To them that's what makes a hero, and that's someone who gets punched so many times but still gets up. So they keep finding new ways to kick his butt but this one was brutal, and a really good examination into his nature and his values."

What better way to knock Steve down than for Doom to kill Cap's original wingman? (And perhaps we should also be worried for Steve's son too, especially as the suggestion is that Doom is seeking revenge for the loss of his own loved ones .)

Of course, nothing yet is certain — and next year's Avengers: Secret Wars is expected to provide something of another MCU reset, meaning any death in Doomsday may not necessarily prove permanent. Still, thinking back to Avengers: Endgame, a few of its biggest deaths have been left as-is so as to not undermine their impact — something a tragic fate for Bucky would likely also qualify for.

The fate of the multiverse — and one James Buchanan "Bucky" Barnes — will be revealed when Avengers: Doomsday opens in theaters on December 18.

articles.title: Disney’s Latest Original Animated Movie Hexed Is Borrowing From a Lot of Better Films
articles.summary: Review: Disney’s latest original animated feature Hexed is borrowing from a lot of better films.
articles.body:
Since the 100th anniversary of Disney Animation in 2023, The Walt Disney Company has released two feature animation sequels, Moana 2 (2024) and Zootopia 2 (2025), and two originals, Wish (2023) and now Hexed. That’s certainly on brand with Disney’s current focus on making sequels to their hits, but not one of that pack rise to the level of game-changing for the historic animation studio. Though Hexed gets points for having an original story by Josie Trinidad (Zootopia+) and screenplay by studio CCO Jared Bush and Dana Ledoux Miller, it’s not conjuring for the fences with its less than fresh storytelling, typical computer-generated imagery, or CGI house style.

Directed by next generation Disney creatives Fawn Veerasunthorn (Wish) and Jason Hand (Moana 2), Hexed centers on rebellious 16-year-old Billie Doe (Hailee Steinfeld) and her helicopter mother Alice Doe (Rashida Jones). They live in the drabbest corner of Ohio where Alice has Billie on a tight leash regarding her every move, even when it comes to growing certain plants in her room (no, not that plant). As revealed in the prologue, Billie was born with magical powers and their manifestation so freaked Alice out that she created a magic suppression bracelet Billie’s been required to wear ever since. The kind-authoritarian parenting approach has left Billie feeling like her mom hates her and goosed her rebellious side, resulting in an expulsion for freeing the school’s owl mascot.

Most importantly, Billie’s caper caused her bracelet to break, sparking up her long dormant powers and bringing forth a plant-based portal that drags her into the magical world of Hexe. This secret dimension was created by witches after the Salem witch trials and it’s filled with a cacophony of witches of all ages, animal Familiars, and Disney-fied hawkers that delight Billie and provide the basics on spell-casting – namely Intention, Ignition and Inwitchification. Playing around with her powers, Billie levitates and flies, which is only done by their ruler, Queen Celeste (Jodie Foster), and quickly gains the monarch’s attention and ire. But Type-A Alice is on the case and follows Billie to Hexe, revealing that she too is a witch and wants her daughter back in Ohio.

What ensues is an overly complicated quest which exposes that Hexe has been under the queen’s kind-authoritarian rule for years. She’s aggressively territorial about her power, so Billie and Alice are threats to her status quo and an impending spell ceremony that’s supposed to lock up her power base. Is it a surprise to find out that she’s got a deeper history with Alice too? Not really, but it explains why Alice fled her magical home when she was pregnant with Billie and has been in hiding ever since.

Hexed is firmly rooted in Disney’s corny and wholesome kind of comedy, drowning its audience in groaner dad jokes and bad puns like, “Witch, please.” Though Billie is classified a rebel, her only “sins” are stealing her mom’s car and calling something crappy once. She’s a good kid in the Disney princess way, and spends most of her road-tripping in Hexe bonding with Alice’s abandoned, three-eyed cat Familiar Beef Roger Crummchuk (Walton Goggins), an enchanted cast iron cauldron named Bucket and, eventually, her mom. Not exactly Violet from Arcane behavior (whom Steinfeld also voices), but maybe it's edgy for Disney-loving households.

Hexed can boast proudly about its sumptuous production design by Lorelay Bove, featuring rich colors and lighting that results in some arresting visuals and environments to look at during the trio’s travels. Goggins is also a standout and a hoot as the crusty cat Beef. However, the rest of the “original” aspects of Hexed are actually heavily borrowed from other films like Howl’s Moving Castle, Kubo and the Two Strings, Wicked, and many, many others. There’s even some purple palette swiping from the demon Saja Boys in KPop Demon Hunters. And interestingly, Hexed and the recent adaptation of The Cat in the Hat share similar storylines about children gaining empathy for the sacrifices of their parents. However, the latter handles it in a far more interesting and emotional way than the heavy-handed approach Hexed takes with Billie, Alice and Celeste. All of it makes for a muddled story, with several sequences and characters that don’t make a lot of narrative sense in general.

As for the animation itself, Hexed has two sequences where the animators break from their CGI norms — a short, 2D shadow play prologue and then a dream state that’s rendered with a misty, brush-stroke overlay. Neither push what their animators can do stylistically or technically. They’re way too subtle, implying that Disney could embrace stylization like the animators do at Dreamworks, Sony Animation and DNEG, who fully committed to mixing up their CGI animation years ago.

Sound-wise, beware that Hexed is a loud one. Much like DreamWork’s Forgotten Island , this film embraces a cacophony of shouting characters and aggressive layers of environmental sounds along with quick cutting that’s meant to hold attention spans but is quite exhausting by the end. Add the astonishingly on-the-nose needle drops layered throughout, and Hexed could be accused of leaning far too much on aural tricks, rather than slowing down and trusting its own storytelling.

Hexed isn’t a bad film, but it’s underwhelming and doesn’t plant a flag of innovation animation-wise. Instead, it's just fine with being an attractive, broad comedy that probably won’t linger in audience minds much after the credits.

articles.title: Everything You Need to Know About HyperX’s Cloud III S and Cloud Alpha Air Headsets
articles.body:
The holidays are nearly here and we’re in the midst of some huge video game releases, so now is a great time to upgrade your gaming setup or help your loved one upgrade theirs. That includes your headset, which doesn’t always get the attention it deserves but can make a big difference to your gaming experience. HyperX remains one of the premiere options for headsets, headlined by the Cloud III S and Cloud Alpha Air.

The HyperX Cloud III S is a wireless headset that adds to the foundation laid by its predecessors in the popular Cloud III line. It’s able to pair with more devices thanks to having connectivity via 2.4GHz wireless, Bluetooth, or an Instant Pair mode that’s compatible with certain OMEN laptops. It’s compatible with PC, Mac, PlayStation 4/5, Nintendo Switch, and mobile, so it covers most devices you’d want to use it with.

One of its defining features is its long battery life, which anyone can tell you is vitally important in a wireless headset. The convenience of going wireless doesn’t do a lot of good if you’re constantly having to recharge it. Luckily, the Cloud III S can reach up to 120 hours of gameplay when connected by 2.4GHz or up to a whopping 200 hours in Bluetooth mode on a single charge.

Wearing it for that long also means it needs to be comfortable, and the Cloud III S has you covered there too. It uses memory foam in the headband for extra padding, and its ear cushions are wrapped in soft leatherette to keep them fitting snugly and comfortably, even during long gaming sessions.

On the tech side, it has 53mm angled drivers to help it deliver clear sound and enhanced audio positioning, which helps you identify audio cues like footsteps. And it has a 10mm boom microphone with an LED mute indicator and built-in mesh filter for clear voice chats and calls.

There are also easy-to-use audio controls, letting you quickly and easily mute and unmute the mic, adjust volume levels, and switch between wireless modes. Plus, the boom mic is detachable and there are two built-in internal mics, so you have the flexibility of ditching the extended mic arm if you want. And it’s compatible with HyperX NGENUITY, which is a software that gives you control of lots of different customization options, like sound profiles, spatial audio, bass levels, and more.

Those are the main benefits of the Cloud III S, while the Cloud Alpha Air brings other strengths to the table. It’s an open-back headset, meaning its earcups are perforated to let sound pass out the back. This offers a totally different audio experience, with a much more natural, expansive soundstage.

Open-back headsets often have to sacrifice the bass, but the Cloud Alpha Air doesn’t have those same limitations. It uses HyperX Bass Tube to maintain the low end while still delivering the more life-like audio that open-back headsets are capable of, giving you the best of both worlds.

The open-back design helps with comfort too, since it’s more breathable and prevents buildup of heat and moisture. That significantly reduces ear fatigue, and when combined with its Ultrasuede materials and plush padding, it keeps them comfortable through extended use. All of that also helps with long-term durability, which is aided by the headset’s metal-reinforced headband and sliders.

It has ports for USB-C, USB-A, 3.5mm, and a USB dongle, allowing it to connect to PCs, Macs, PlayStation 4/5, and Xbox Series X|S. And like its cousin, it’s also compatible with NGENUITY, letting you get down to the nitty gritty details to find what works best for you.

If a new headset is on your holiday shopping list, then the HyperX Cloud III S and HyperX Cloud Alpha Air both make great options. It just comes down to personal preferences. articles.title: Marvel Shows Off First Look at Kelsey Grammer's Beast in Avengers: Doomsday, and Fans Are Divided
articles.summary: We’ve gotten our first look at Kelsey Grammer’s Beast as he will appear in Avengers: Doomsday, prompting fan confusion about why Marvel waited so long to reveal him and comparisons to his appearance at the end of The Marvels.
articles.body:
We’ve gotten our first look at Kelsey Grammer’s Beast as he will appear in Avengers: Doomsday, prompting fan confusion about why Marvel waited so long to reveal him and sparking comparisons to his appearance at the end of The Marvels.

This first look comes courtesy of Entertainment Weekly , which shared a high-resolution image of the furry blue mutant looking on with a mystified expression. The outlet’s report states that Kelsey Grammer was the second X-Men veteran to join the cast of Doomsday following the late great Patrick Stewart , making his first comeback appearance in a post-credits scene in The Marvels.

Apparently, Grammer’s scene was so well-received that Marvel decided to bring him back for their upcoming Avengers adventure. EW says that Grammer was told that he received “a lot of great response from that little cameo" — a sentiment that fans echoed in comments across social media.

First look at Kelsey Grammer as Beast in ‘AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY’. (Source: — DiscussingFilm (@DiscussingFilm) November 24, 2026

First look at Kelsey Grammer as Beast in ‘AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY’. (Source:

Most were puzzled as to why Marvel waited so long to show off the character, though some are at odds with his updated design in comparison to how he looked in The Marvels.

“Why were they so reluctant to show Beast fully, he actually doesn’t even look bad?” one confused commenter wrote.

“Looks way better than he did in The Marvels, why were they hiding him?” another asked.

“I like it, even though his appearance in The Marvels looked better,” yet another posited.

Avengers: Doomsday Poster Montage Gallery

This film will mark the fourth time Grammer has portrayed Beast; he first took up the mantle in 2006's X-Men: The Last Stand , and reprised the role in X-Men: Days of Future Past in 2014. Almost a decade after this, he once again appeared as the character in 2023's The Marvels, and will once again play the part in Avengers: Doomsday in just a few weeks' time.

IGN got the chance to speak with Grammer after Days of Future Past, who told us he would "love" to do another X-Men movie. "I loved playing the Beast," he told us. "I called him the Blue Guy. It was just a joy for me to be involved in that franchise.

"Actually, when I heard they were making another one, it was Hugh [Jackman]. I was talking to him, and somebody said, 'Oh, you're going to be in the next one, mate.' And I said, 'Well, I didn't even know about it.'"

A slew of characters have already been confirmed to appear in Avengers: Doomsday. A recent trailer for the film showed off a few of the teams we can expect to throw down in the movie, which, of course, includes the X-Men. And a new poster also gave fans an up-close-and-personal look at Doctor Doom's metal mask, which some fans can't help but compare to another Marvel poster of Iron Man.

articles.title: Rings of Power Renewed by Amazon for Season 4
articles.summary: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 wraps up later tonight, but the show has already been renewed for Season 4 at Prime Video.
articles.body:
The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 wraps up later tonight, but the show has already been renewed for Season 4 at Prime Video.

Amazon MGM has renewed Rings of Power just as the show has wrapped up its third season, according to a report from Variety . The new season will continue the show's exploration of Middle-earth's second age, and will begin filming in spring 2027, though no release date has been announced yet.

While the show has been divisive for Tolkien fans, Amazon MGM's head of global television, Peter Friedlander, tells Variety that, "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power has become a defining series for Prime Video." He also says that after the finale of Season 3 delivered "the landmark moment fans have been waiting for," the studio looks forward to "bringing fans even deeper into the rich world of Tolkien's Second Age."

The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 Theo / Nazgnagôl Photos

Thus far, the third season seems to be an improvement. Here at IGN, we gave the last three episodes of the show a 7 out of 10, with reviewer Jim Vejvoda saying, "The Rings of Power loses some forward momentum this week with two very talky episodes where several characters are literally waiting around for something to happen." However, the first half of the season was much stronger, with Jim giving the first four episodes an 8 , saying "The Rings of Power Season 3, Episodes 1-4 prove a welcome return to Middle-earth, allowing the series to get back on track after two seasons of wandering."

However, as the show nears the war that ends the Second Age of Middle-earth, it's going to be interesting to see where the showrunners take Rings of Power next season. There is a good chunk of time between the forging of the One Ring and the War of the Last Alliance that kicked off the Third Age, but no matter where they go with it, it'll likely involve the expanding influence of Sauron. We might even get another time jump.

It'll also be interesting to see if Prime Video takes the same approach to the show's release as it did with Season 3, releasing the episodes in blocks of three, likely to lure in new subscribers during Black Friday. articles.title: Walmart Now Lets Meta’s Muse AI Agent Shop for You During Black Friday
articles.body:
Ready or not, the world of agentic AI is descending upon us. From Meta’s Muse to OpenAI’s Dots , a number of artificial intelligence companies have released digital “agents” that have capabilities beyond just answering questions in a chat window. These AI assistants can actually do things for you, either in the cloud or directly on your computer. One of those things is shopping.

Some retailers are putting up barriers to make sure AI bots can’t shop on their websites. Walmart is going the other way and embracing the AI-bot-shopping future. Just in time for Black Friday , the mega-retailer has set up Agent Profiles and the Walmart Agent Gateway , which allow digital agents to shop on behalf of customers, within certain limitations. Muse intigration with your Walmart account is now available.

With Agent Profiles, Walmart’s system knows your Muse agent is shopping on your behalf, and won’t mistake its actions for yours. The profile also lets you track which items your agent has purchased separately from those you've bought yourself.

Muse won’t have access to your shopping history or other personal information known to Walmart. You can set additional guardrails around your Muse agent, like giving it a spending limit, and requiring it to ask for manual approval before completing purchases. You can also delete the agent’s profile at any time.

If you want to try it out, you can do so in the Muse app. First you’ll be asked to sign into your Walmart account, and then brought back to Muse, where you can ask it to compare products or find deals on items you’re interested in buying. It can add items to your cart and use your saved payment information to check out, if you let it.

I tried the Walmart integration this morning by asking Muse to add an item to my cart. Instead of using the official Walmart Agent Gateway and creating an Agent Profile, it opened a virtual browser and added the item to a guest cart on Walmart's site, set for pickup at a store I didn’t recognize.

I then asked Muse if it had official Walmart integration, and it confirmed that it did. Only then did it offer me the new sign-in option. So you may need to specifically ask for it if you want to try it yourself.

On the other hand, if you want to do it old-school and peruse Walmart's Black Friday 2026 sale personally and without an AI agent, I don't blame you one bit.

articles.title: Kevin Feige and the Russo Brothers are Planning a Special Tribute to Patrick Stewart as Avengers: Doomsday Release Approaches
articles.summary: Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige has revealed that he and the Russo brothers are creating a tribute to honor the late great Patrick Stewart in light of his final performance in Avengers: Doomsday.
articles.body:
Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige has revealed that he and the Russo brothers are creating a tribute to honor the late great Patrick Stewart in light of his final performance in Avengers: Doomsday.

Sir Patrick Stewart died at the age of 86 on October 28, 2026. The prolific actor’s death followed a brief battle with Alzheimer's and Lewy Body Dementia, prompting a period of mourning from both fans and fellow collaborators, the latter of whom shared fond memories from their time working with the Star Trek and X-Men alum on social media.

Speaking with Entertainment Weekly ahead of Avengers: Doomsday’s December release, Kevin Feige revealed that he and the Russo brothers are working on creating a tribute to Stewart, given his many years playing Charles Xavier in the X-Men films.

“We’re long done filming that movie [Doomsday], and he did an amazing job for us,” Feige told the outlet. “We’re looking now at how we can put something together that honors and respects our friend.”

In that same interview, Joseph Russo reflected on Stewart’s role in the upcoming film, revealing that the actor shared a particularly moving scene with his fellow thespian and real-life best friend, Ian McKellan. (I’m growing misty-eyed as I type this; McKellan shared a touching statement about his late friend shortly after the news broke, saying he “wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and in my case, love.")

“In a lot of ways, Xavier’s the conscience in the movie,” Joseph Russo revealed. “He has a lovely scene with Ian McKellen, who’s his best friend, in the film. It’s a very emotional scene about forgiveness, and I think very resonant in the wake of his passing.”

Anthony Russo went on to share an anecdote about his time working with Stewart on the set of Doomsday, saying the actor did his best to put on a good show in spite of his failing health.

“It was clear that he was struggling with his health, and he worked so hard to deliver a performance and a presence — for us as directors, for his other actors, for the crew,” Anthony said. “You could see it wasn’t just the effort of a regular actor showing up and delivering that kind of presence and performance and experience for others, collaboration. It was someone who was really being challenged in a very deep way on a health level, showing up and doing that. For him to have muscled through and delivered the performance that he did in that movie, and the experience that he delivered for all of us as collaborators, it made it intensely emotional.”

Avengers: Doomsday marks Patrick Stewart’s final film performance. The knighted actor was best known for playing Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek and Charles Xavier in the X-Men films of the 2010s, but also lent his talents to numerous memorable voiceover roles, such as Emperor Uriel Septim VII in the Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion and Lord Yupa in Studio Ghibli’s Nausicaa of the Valley of the Wind .

Avengers: Doomsday releases in theaters on December 18, 2026. For more news about this forthcoming superhero flick, check out what we learned from its “final” trailer , and peep the parallels fans discovered between the latest Doctor Doom poster and another early promotional Iron Man poster.

articles.title: PlayStation Secures Marketing Agreement for The Witcher 4
articles.summary: CD Projekt Red has signed a marketing deal with PlayStation for The Witcher 4.
articles.body:
CD Projekt Red has signed a marketing deal with PlayStation for The Witcher 4 .

The studio confirmed the deal in its latest earnings report, which may also suggest that marketing is about to ramp up. Additionally, CD Projekt Red noted that this partnership will "cover the presence" of its games on PlayStation and PlayStation Plus, which likely means older titles like The Witcher 3 or Cyberpunk 2077 may make their way to the subscription service in the future.

“Just today, we signed new partnership agreements with Sony Interactive Entertainment covering the presence of our games on PlayStation and in PlayStation Plus subscriptions, as well as our collaboration during the upcoming Witcher 4 marketing campaign,” said Piotr Nielubowicz, chief financial officer at CDPR. "This cooperation will support our business and financial outlook in this and future years.”

The Witcher IV Game Awards Trailer Screenshots

It wouldn't be surprising if PlayStation uses this agreement to make The Witcher 3 available through PlayStation Plus when the game's new expansion releases in 2027. This deal may also mean that The Witcher 4 has a big presence in a future State of Play stream, though no hard specifics were revealed by CD Projekt Red. Currently, the game is due out in 2028 , so new trailers and gameplay seem likely next year.

The decision also signals an end of an era, to a degree. CD Projekt Red has had a strong relationship with Xbox since The Witcher 3. The game was prominently featured during Xbox's E3 showcases, and that continued with Cyberpunk 2077, even resulting in a special edition Xbox One X console themed after the game. Given PlayStation has a larger user base than Xbox this generation, it makes sense why CDPR may be interested in working with them.

Marketing deals can be extremely effective when done right. In the case of GTA 6, a lot of people bought PlayStation 5s instead of an Xbox, since Rockstar and Sony marketed the console as the "best place to play" the game. This led to the game being the biggest launch in PlayStation's history , with 39 million people playing it on PS5. 70% of people who bought a new PS5 during the last week also booted up GTA 6 as their first game.

articles.title: Cyberpunk 2 Is Still a Ways Out, but CD Projekt Red Says Its RPGs Will Come Out Faster in the Future
articles.summary: We are still two years out from The Witcher 4, but Ciri's big breakout adventure isn't the only massive RPG cooking at CD Projekt Red. It sounds like development on Cyberpunk 2 is carrying on smoothly, though it's still very early in its development cycle.
articles.body:
We are still two years out from The Witcher 4 , but Ciri's big breakout adventure isn't the only massive RPG cooking at CD Projekt Red. It sounds like development on Cyberpunk 2 is carrying on smoothly, though it's still very early in its development cycle.

In a November 24 earnings call , CD Projekt Red VP of Strategy & Investor Relations Karolina Gnaś said the team is "making good progress with Cyberpunk 2, we are happy with where we are, but it's still too early to give a specific date and plan on when we will move onto full production." Although she couldn't provide a clear date when we'll hear more about the game, she did add that the studio plans to have around 200 developers by the end of 2026 and 320 by the end of next year.

It is admittedly a bit early to expect any kind of information about the Cyberpunk sequel, but it has been simmering in the background since at least 2022 , and it sounds like CD Projekt Red wants to speed up development of its massive RPGs. In its consolidated earnings report , CD Projekt Red admitted that most of its games "normally take 3 to 6 years to produce," mostly due to working on one game at a time. But that strategy has since changed.

In that same report, the company said, "At the moment, the CD Projekt Red studio is working in parallel on several productions (also in collaboration with external development teams) and supporting products, which is expected to translate into shorter intervals between the releases of subsequent titles in the future." Whether or not that new timeline will affect Cyberpunk 2 is the question.

But even if that faster development timeline is in effect for Cyberpunk 2, it's likely we'll still have to wait a while to actually see it in the wild. In an earnings report last year, when Cyberpunk 2 entered pre-production, CD Projekt CEO Michał Nowakowski suggested that CDPR's games take four or five years to move from pre-production to release, which would put the game somewhere in 2030 or 2031. And given that the game still hasn't entered full production, it isn't likely we're going to see some sort of rapid release after the Witcher 4 in 2028.

We're probably going to be waiting a little while longer for Cyberpunk 2, but it's already sounding like the game is taking shape. Just last month, associate game director Pawel Sasko revealed that a lot of the developers working on Cyberpunk 2 are former modders. Sasko went on to claim that "the modding community is really keeping [Cyberpunk 2077] alive," so hopefully that energy translates to Cyberpunk 2 – whenever it comes out.

articles.title: 'Crazy Secretive' — GTA 6 Voice Actor Reveals Details of Rockstar's 'Humongous' NDA
articles.summary: A voice actor who appeared in GTA 6 described the wild non-disclosure agreement she had to sign before working on the game, calling the project “crazy secretive.”
articles.body:
A voice actor who appeared in GTA 6 described the wild non-disclosure agreement she had to sign before working on the game, calling the project “crazy secretive.”

Issa Lopez is a voice actor who plays a radio host on GTA 6’s fictional Cocoteo FM radio station, a Latin channel that plays reggaeton and dembow tracks featuring Spanish-speaking artists from the Caribbean and Latin America.

In a November 20 interview with Page Six , Lopez revealed that she recorded her lines for the station as recently as September 2026, and said the NDA she was made to sign before officially performing the part was comparable to the process of purchasing a home or a vehicle.

“Have you ever signed papers to buy a house? To buy a car? You know, it’s thick! It was a pretty humongous pack of papers that came with it. But I mean, it’s worth it! And I didn’t have to wait like all these other folks. Some of these folks have been working on this for like 10–11 years, you know what I mean?” she said.

She went on to describe the recording process for her lines, saying that she hadn’t seen anything until the day of the performance. With no time to prepare, she was essentially “put on the spot” — but she was so excited about the opportunity that she didn’t mind.

“In my usual voiceover gigs — let’s say you want me to do a commercial for you. I get a Zoom [link] maybe the day before, maybe the same day I get the script,” she explained. “Everything was like, popped up on the screen. It was mad cool. It was like, ‘You ready? And I’m like, ‘Uh-huh.’ You press a button and then boop, it pops on the screen, they say hello, and there’s a bunch of people in your ear. And they’re like, ‘Okay, here it is,’ and that’s when you see it. You are put on the spot. And you better bring it. And after that, I don’t know — whatever was in front of my face disappeared. “

Lopez revealed that she wasn’t told what the project was for, but figured it out based on context clues from an email titled “heard by millions,” saying she “read it and knew what it was for.” She also didn’t know that Bad Bunny would be co-hosting the Cocoteo station alongside her, leading to a wild realization once Rockstar released the radio stations before the game actually came out.

“We knew nothing. I saw the liners, and when I saw the liners I was like, ‘Okay, I know why I got the gig.’ ‘Cause it was like Puerto Rican dot com. It was super easy. But it was so cool, because Rockstar let me be myself. …they were like, ‘Issa, we want natural. Whatever you got, we want,'" she said.

The actors in GTA 6 were extremely secretive about their involvement in the project. Most notably, actress Manni L. Perez, who plays Lucia, was under immense pressure after fans sleuthed her social media accounts and figured out it was her before she could officially reveal the information. Now, she’s up for best performance at The Game Awards, which is one of eight nominations the game has secured mere weeks before the show takes place this December.

Other performers who have finally revealed their involvement in the game are Mandy’s actress, Lexie Shoaibi , as well as the voice and performance artist for Jason Duval, Dylan Rourke . Rockstar released the full credits for the game, too, which you can check out here — just beware of spoilers if you haven’t finished it yet.

If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips , Chapter 2 Guide and Tips , and Chapter 3 Guide and Tips . If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map .

articles.title: The Witcher 4 Will Have a Comparable Leap From GTA 5 to GTA 6, Says CD Projekt Red
articles.summary: CD Projekt Red expects a leap between The Witcher 3 and 4 that is comparable to the one between GTA 5 and 6.
articles.body:
CD Projekt Red expects a leap between The Witcher 3 and 4 that is comparable to the one between GTA 5 and 6.

In a recent earnings call (via Eurogamer ), CDPR was peppered with questions about GTA 6, since the developer also makes ambitious open-world games. CDPR joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski was asked whether or not the studio is looking at GTA for inspiration and if people can expect a similar leap between games. He noted that they have, indeed, observed the jump between GTA 5 and 6 before stating that fans can expect something comparable for The Witcher 4.

"We believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 — I think so, yes," he said. "It's been 11 years, we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes, you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4."

The Witcher 4 Unreal Engine 5 Tech Demo Screenshots

The leap between GTA 5 and 6 is pretty absurd. There's a significant number of more things to do, particularly for those interested in roleplaying as a criminal. You can steal drugs, rob banks, knock over virtually any store on the map, and so much more. A lot of these details were either reserved for scripted missions in GTA 5 or were underbaked as open-world activities, but are fully fleshed out for you to do however you want in GTA 6. Advancements in NPCs, interactivity, immersion, and the ability to enter hundreds of interiors also make GTA 6 feel a world apart from its predecessor.

Will The Witcher 4 also have tons of enterable interiors or deeper interactions with random NPCs? It's too soon to tell. It's possible that the leap for CD Projekt Red could come in a number of other ways, as The Witcher is a totally different world from GTA, after all. Maybe monster hunting will be more nuanced and involved than in The Witcher 3, similar to how GTA 6 has more engaging criminal activities.

CDPR also noted that it plans to find ways to expand the game to more mainstream audiences, like GTA 6 has. GTA 6 collaborated with major mainstream artists to create original music, in addition to bold marketing campaigns that made the game difficult to ignore.

The Witcher 4 is currently targeting a 2028 release , and we can probably expect more looks at the game next year. CDPR also noted that it has signed a marketing agreement with PlayStation for the game, which will also cover previous games and allow for opportunities with PlayStation Plus' services.

articles.title: Diablo 4 Season 16 Fixes One of the Biggest Problems With Helltide
articles.summary: Diablo 4 Season 16: Season of Tyrael's Gambit officially kicks off on December 1. We finally know a bit more about what the new season holds in store, and it's going to make one of the biggest activities much less of a pain.
articles.body:
Diablo 4 Season 16: Season of Tyrael's Gambit officially kicks off on December 1. We finally know a bit more about what the new season holds in store, and it's going to make one of the biggest activities much less of a pain.

Season 15, Hell's Legacy, is a tough act to follow. It brought in a ton of nostalgic content like the Prime Evils, runewords, and even Whimsyshire. It does seem like a lot of that anniversary content is going to be retired (I'll miss runewords), but at least it seems like Season of Tyrael's Gambit is going to make farming Helltides a bit less annoying.

In the patch notes for the new season , Blizzard says one Helltide will always be up in the vanilla zones, with another active in either Nahantu or Skovos, offset by 30 minutes. In practice, that means there will always be an active Helltide. That would be good enough on its own, but Blizzard is also changing the way Abberant Cinders work. Instead of expiring at the end of each Helltide, Blizzard is introducing a cap, and will let you carry cinders between Helltides.

For the uninitiated, that might not seem like a big deal, but it's a massive quality-of-life change. If you're not aware, Helltide is essentially an in-game invasion event, where demons overrun an area in the open world. You go in and kill demons for 55 minutes to get Abberant Cinders, which you can then use to unlock chests scattered throughout the zone. Helltides have always been one of the best ways to farm XP, and there have been several seasons that revolve entirely around them.

Now that War Plans, which were introduced with Lord of Hatred, are such a central part of how Diablo 4's gameplay loop works, there's always a chance that you're going to need to do bit of Helltide farming to progress. The problem was that Helltides spawned on a timer, and there was always a 5-minute gap between them. That doesn't sound too bad, but sometimes a Helltide would pop up in your to-do list and you'd either zone in with a mere 10 minutes to gather a ton of Cinders, or there simply wouldn't be a Helltide active. This new change solves both of those problems.

Now, even if you go into a Helltide with just a few minutes remaining, you can still gather Cinders without having to worry about opening 250 Cinders worth of chests before the timer expires. You can simply farm until the Helltide moves and then teleport to the next one. Easy. It's such a seemingly small change, but it's made me more excited for the 16th season of this ARPG than anything I've heard about it so far.

Beyond that, the Season of Tyrael's Gambit also brings changes to War Plans, where you'll be able to customize them to favor the activities you actually like doing. So, if you hate Helltide, even with the new changes, it sounds like you'll be able to make them appear a little less often in your War Plans.

The new season will also have a new item type called Horadric Items, which will synergize with set talismans. In the example Blizzard shared in its post, this could be as simple as adding +1 set count to your talismans to an ability that is only activated if you have a certain set of talismans equipped.

Seasons like this are a prime example of the way Blizzard will support Diablo 4 going forward, now that Diablo 5 is in the works. Diablo 4's director has come out and reassured fans that the game will continue to get new seasons as long as people are playing , and with how different Diablo 5 sounds so far , it's possible that Diablo 4 will have a long life ahead of it.

articles.title: GTA VI PC recompilation project shut down by Take-Two
articles.summary: Modders are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC.
articles.body: Game modding communities are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC, but one big effort has been taken down by Take-Two today. Leonida, a fan project by 15-year-old “NotRexed,” has vanished after a DMCA takedown notice from GTA VI publisher Take-Two. Leonida was designed to translate a leaked GTA VI Xbox build to run natively on Windows. Cyberleek, the leaker who posted multiple GTA VI gameplay videos over the summer, published a full Xbox build of the game earlier this week. The leak has kicked recompilation efforts up a notch, as modders race to reverse-engineer the game’s code and rebuild it into native PC code. Some have managed to get the game to boot on PC, but recompiling the full game won’t be easy — even with help from AI tools like Claude. Take-Two is trying to slow this progress, and its IP enforcement team targeted the main GitHub repository for Leonida and more than 2,900 forks of it, claiming that it “infringes upon Take-Two’s copyrighted works and facilitates copyright infringement of Rockstar Games title, Grand Theft Auto VI.” PortWatch VI is tracking the efforts to recompile, emulate, or port the leaked Xbox build over to PC. At the time of publishing, the VIctory project and forks of it are leading the way. People are also trying to use XCL, a compatibility layer that runs Xbox Series X games on a Windows PC, to get GTA VI running. At this point, it seems like Take-Two might not be able to avoid the inevitable here. The clock started ticking down to the release of the PC version last week, and if recent reports are true, we might see it in a few months. If GTA VI is close to being officially ready for PC, we could hear about a release before modders manage to get the game running on PC unofficially.

articles.title: Some GTA 6 Fans Love Chapter 1 for Its Slower Pace and Are Spending Dozens of Hours Roleplaying in It
articles.summary: GTA 6's first chapter has been somewhat divisive due to its slower pace, but it's also a part of the game that some fans have spent dozens of hours playing due to it highly immersive slice-of-life elements.
articles.body:
Warning: This article features light spoilers for the early hours of GTA 6 .

GTA 6's first chapter has been somewhat divisive due to its slower pace, but it's also a part of the game that some fans have spent dozens of hours playing due to it highly immersive slice-of-life elements.

Instead of throwing you headfirst into crazy heists or explosive set pieces, the first chapter of GTA 6 is largely spent bumbling around Rockstar's version of the Florida Keys. You can go fishing, scuba diving, and even fix up your house before Lucia's release from prison. It's an exceptionally low-key and chill opening to a game filled with all kinds of crazy action, which is why it's also rubbed some people the wrong way. They don't want to do chores or kick it on the beach; they want to cause some mayhem.

However, for others, this has become an unexpected hook for GTA 6 that actually delayed their interest in getting to the meat of Rockstar's open-world epic. Various fans of the game have said they spent anywhere from 10 to as many as 40+ hours in just Chapter 1 alone. Keep in mind, this is a sliver of the overall experience, and much of the game's most interesting activities don't get added until subsequent chapters. However, some players just enjoyed living inside of this part of the game before things go horribly wrong and they're forced to start ramping up the violence and crime.

"Best thing about that early chapter is just how low stakes and casual it feels," said X user @CS11__ after spending 41 hours in Chapter 1 alone. "I forced myself not to go farther than Hamlet, so I really only ever experienced these two small areas in 40 hours. [...] The game hardly opened up, but it still felt unbelievably rich and fun."

But... what is it these people are actually doing, if not blowing stuff up and creating tons of chaos? Some fans were just going through the motions, giving themselves daily routines that involved working out, taking on relaxing hobbies, and exploring.

"[A] lot of roleplaying, day-to-day living type stuff," said Aaron Espionza on X , who estimated that he spent around 15–18 hours before picking up Lucia from prison. "I had a routine even when I would wake up, drive to the juice bar down the street, get my orange juice, and then say hello to the locals. If anyone said anything mean, I would get violent and throw empty juice cups at them. [I] did the workout routines. Basketball was a favorite of mine. Side stuff with Cal fishing, Donnie pick-ups, and scuba. But so much of it was testing how much detail Rockstar put into it. 'If I do this , will they do that ?' type of systems exploration. Always came away surprised."

X user @scaasm noted that the lower stakes nature of Chapter 1 even prompted him to follow traffic laws and use manual turn signals in GTA 6: "I follow traffic laws unless I'm doing something criminal, and generally just taking it very slow. [I'm] loving every moment."

The location itself was also a big driving point for a lot of fans, some of whom have personal connections or apprecation for its real life counterpart: "As someone from Florida, I think the Keys is one of those locations that they absolutely nailed (waning sands outlets too; they look exactly like the Orlando ones)," said @piterparker69 on X . "It felt kinda uncanny driving around (especially the 7 Mile Bridge) because of how good it replicates real life."

"I have been obsessed with the Florida Keys for the last 5 years, and finding out you spend the start of the game there, catching fish, fixing my house, working out, and just vibing gave me little motivation to move on," said @AnchormanV2 on X after spending roughly a dozen hours in Chapter 1.

"I took my sweet time in Key Lento, not necessarily to avoid progressing the story, but more so [bcause] I was just having so much fun exploring the keys and just taking it all in," said X user @HorrorUntitled . "There’s just so much to see to see and happening. It’s very overwhelming."

Of course, some people did get into a bit of open-world crime as well, or explore a bit beyond the Keys, but a lot of it was still a result of the story feeling low-stakes and not having much urgency in its first chaper. X user Ryan Ranc even noted that he would go around Key Lento acting as a vigilante: "I’m playing as Batman and roaming at night on my motorbike stopping crime."

Chapter 1 in GTA 6 is a very interesting piece of the game, and some even noted that they longed for that tranquility after moving on in the story. It's an intentional slow burn, as things get turned up to an 11 at the end of the chapter and make you come to appreciate what you had. It's the calm before the storm in many ways, and some people are really basking in that.
